as_of_note: Snapshot pulls Fri Nov 13, 2026, about 8:35-8:45am PT. Kalshi pull 12:00pm PT. The daily research package carries the newer read.

decision.summary: The FOMC meets Dec 8-9 with the target range at 3.75-4.00% after a 10-2 October hold in which Cook and Hammack dissented for an immediate hike. The call is a 25bp hike on Dec 9: core PCE, the variable the 2% target is defined on, runs 3.12% y/y; the labor market shows no deterioration on any kept read; growth runs above trend; and Kalshi prices a hike at $1.00 combined ($0.88 for 25bp, $0.12 for more, pulled 12:00 PT). Confidence is high on direction, indicators and markets agree, and lower on size: the 50bp tail repriced from $0.05 in the morning to $0.12, and no indicator rule distinguishes 25bp from 50bp. November CPI lands Dec 10 (date single-basis), after the decision, so it cannot change December. The decision belongs to the Committee.

lines: The 10-year yield (FRED DGS10) rose 4.86% (Nov 6) to 4.98% (Nov 10). At assumed perpetual growth g = 3.00%, the Gordon multiple 1 / (r - g) falls 53.76x to 50.51x, down 6.06%. Arithmetic, not opinion.
That is a multiple change: Mr. Market repricing the same earnings stream at a higher discount rate. Earnings power did not change on any data in this session's pulls.
Duration of about 8 puts the same +12bp move at about -0.96% on a 10-year position (approximation; ignores convexity).
The margin of safety is thinner at the same prices: any intrinsic-value estimate carried at the old 4.86% anchor overstates value by about 6% on this sensitivity. Re-anchor to 4.98%.
The defensive read: the bond side pays about 5% on a contractual claim, so equity risk must be compensated from price, a wider required discount, not a chase for yield.
graham.spread: Earnings-yield vs bond-yield spread: UNVERIFIED. Bond side verified (4.98%); earnings side unverified from any primary source this session (Shiller download failed; no S&P Dow Jones figure). No live spread is asserted.

grounding: CFA evidence discipline (diligence, reasonable basis, documented record, verdict as thesis, evidence, and what would change it). Broker discipline (reasonable basis, mandate fit, fair-and-balanced presentation including disconfirming evidence) per the repo's derived Series 7 domain notes. No LEM manual text was available to cite. No rule numbers, quotes, or licensed text are reproduced. No license is claimed; this is decision support, not a recommendation.

indicators.broker: Anchor the discount rate to the higher regime. Do not re-anchor on a soft CPI print, the decision variable is PCE, and the next PCE print (Nov 25, date provisional) is the re-anchor date.

gauge.note: m/m +0.317% also fires the HIKE rule (above +0.25%). Gauge uses y/y, the target variable.

indicators.name: Core PCE price index
indicators.trigger: HIKE if y/y above 2.5% or m/m above +0.25%; CUT if y/y below 2.2%.
indicators.why: The 2% target is defined on this series; nothing outranks it.

indicators.broker: Anchored market expectations mean no credibility crisis in the bond market: room for 25bp, not a forced 50bp. The tripwire is a break above 2.75%.

gauge.note: NEUTRAL band 2.0-2.5% per the rule. Both tenors sit inside it.

indicators.name: Breakeven expectations
indicators.trigger: HIKE if above 2.75%; CUT if below 1.75%; NEUTRAL 2.0-2.5%.
indicators.why: Expectations feed wage and price setting; anchored expectations give the Fed room.

indicators.broker: Do not average this with breakevens: 4.3% against 2.24% is a credibility gap the Fed reads as pressure to act. The fall from 4.7% narrows the gap; the level still fires the trigger.

gauge.note: Oct 4.7% to Nov prelim 4.3%. The level still fires the HIKE rule.

indicators.name: Michigan expectations
indicators.trigger: HIKE if year-ahead above 3.5%; CUT if below 2.5%.
indicators.why: Household expectations feed wage demands directly and respond to prices households see.

indicators.broker: Apply the rule as written: NEUTRAL. The single +165k print does not override the average, one print is noise, the average is the signal, and cherry-picking the strong print fails the reasonable-basis standard.

gauge.note: Oct single print +165k does not override the average; the rule reads the average.

indicators.name: Payrolls, 3-month average
indicators.trigger: HIKE if 3-month average above +150k; CUT if below +50k.
indicators.why: The direct count of job creation; the employment half of the mandate.

indicators.broker: No action on this read. Check it every Thursday: it turns first, and a 4-week average above 300k flips the labor read to CUT before payrolls confirm.

gauge.note: No HIKE rule: low claims read NEUTRAL. NEUTRAL below 250k; the CUT tripwire is 300k.

indicators.name: Initial claims, 4-week average
indicators.trigger: CUT if 4-week average above 300k; NEUTRAL below 250k.
indicators.why: The fastest labor signal; claims rise before payrolls fall.

indicators.broker: Demand has not rolled over: this rules out the labor-is-cracking case for a hold. It corroborates payrolls, filled jobs plus unfilled demand, rather than replacing them.

gauge.note: Sep 7,523k minus Jul 7,335k = +188k (arithmetic on the stated levels).

indicators.name: Job openings
indicators.trigger: HIKE if 3-month change positive; CUT if down 500k over 3 months.
indicators.why: Openings measure labor demand; the openings-to-unemployed ratio is the tightness gauge the Fed has cited.

indicators.broker: Above-trend growth removes the restraint-is-biting objection to a hike. Growth is the backdrop, not the trigger. The prints that can move the call before Dec 9 are PCE, claims, and the minutes.
indicators.name: Real GDP
indicators.trigger: HIKE if above 2.5% annualized; CUT if below 1.0%.
indicators.why: Growth above trend with inflation above target means the economy can absorb tighter policy.

indicators.broker: Report it, do not bury it: this is the evidence a hold argument would cite, and it is why the call is 25bp, not 50bp. A view that omits its strongest counter-evidence fails the fair-and-balanced standard.

gauge.note: Down 10.8% Jul to Sep; the CUT rule fires at down 5% over 3 months. The HIKE side (rising through high rates) has no numeric tripwire.

indicators.name: Housing starts
indicators.trigger: CUT if down 5% over 3 months; HIKE if rising through high rates.
indicators.why: The most rate-sensitive sector; the first place transmission shows up.

indicators.broker: No stress: the market is neither doing the Fed's tightening work nor forcing an easing response. No defensive action on credit; the watch is a break above 5.00%.

gauge.note: No HIKE rule. NEUTRAL below 4.00%; the CUT tripwire is 5.00%.

indicators.name: High-yield OAS
indicators.why: The price of credit risk; widening spreads mean conditions tightening on their own.

indicators.broker: Weight the vote above any single print: two dissents for an immediate hike plus that sentence is the Committee stating its lean. The Nov 18 minutes are the check on whether 10-2 understates division.
indicators.name: FOMC vote and guidance
indicators.read: Oct 28: held 3.75-4.00%, 10-2, Cook and Hammack dissenting for +25bp; statement: Inflation remains elevated. 7 hawkish / 0 dovish named statements this week (inference, single-basis press reports).
indicators.trigger: HIKE if dissents favor tightening or statement language turns hawkish; CUT if the reverse.
indicators.why: The Committee speaking for itself outranks any data print.

market_pricing.disagreement: The remaining disagreement is between the markets and the indicators: the indicator set votes direction (hike), not size, and no rule in it distinguishes 25bp from 50bp. The tail repriced intraday, after the morning PPI release (+0.3% m/m reported, y/y +6.5%, BLS USDL 26-1687); no kept indicator printed new data in that window, so the size repricing is market-driven, not data-driven.
market_pricing.fedwatch_note: CME FedWatch could not be read directly (embedded app, no public text API); secondhand reads Nov 10-13 converge at 87-91% for 25bp and 9-15% for 50bp. This morning Kalshi's tail ($0.05) sat below the FedWatch range; it has since repriced to $0.12, inside it. The two markets now agree on direction and tail.
market_pricing.kalshi_note: Kalshi, direct API pull Nov 13, 12:00 PT (Dec-2026 meeting, KXFEDDECISION): 25bp hike $0.88 (bid/ask 0.87/0.88, prev 0.86), more than 25bp $0.12 (0.11/0.12, prev 0.11), hold $0.03, cuts $0.01 each; the five lasts sum to $1.05 (5-cent over-round). Total hike $1.00.

objective: Anchor cross-asset research in Treasury curves, real rates, Fed policy, credit spreads, duration, and liquidity stress.
what_would_change: October core PCE (Nov 25; date single-basis, provisional): m/m at or below +0.15% with a downward revision to September. The target variable softening.
Initial claims 4-week average above 300k. The fast labor signal turning before payrolls confirm.
November 18 minutes, or a named speaker arguing for a hold, showing the Committee more worried about overtightening than the 10-2 vote suggested. Guidance shifting against the hike.
